Needs changes before merge. Safety-tier review. One NEW blocker: a `camcraft-ui` lib test fails on this head.

This review is on the same head as the earlier clean review (comment of 2026-11-25 03:25 UTC). The earlier review could not see the failure: the quick gate plan of this diff has no `camcraft-ui` step (49 steps, `motion` and `app` only). This PR changes no file in `crates/ui`, but it changes `PickCapability::Threading::takes`, and the UI reads that function. So the `merge-ready` label is replaced with `needs-rework`, and the PR is a draft again.

## Earlier findings

The earlier review requested no change. There is nothing to resolve.

## NEW blocker

1. **A UI test fails** - `crates/ui/src/egui_app/start_exit_tests.rs:189` (`egui_app::start_exit_rows::tests::the_wire_geometry_tab_groups_the_start_hole_and_says_the_exit_is_not_taken`).

   ```
   thread 'egui_app::start_exit_rows::tests::the_wire_geometry_tab_groups_the_start_hole_and_says_the_exit_is_not_taken' panicked at crates/ui/src/egui_app/start_exit_tests.rs:189:9:
   Wire Contour has Exit point on Geometry
   test result: FAILED. 1639 passed; 1 failed; 8 ignored
   ```

   Cause: `not_taken_groups` (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/start_exit_rows.rs:110-122`) draws the Exit point group only for a role that the kind does not take. `Threading` now takes the exit, so the Wire Contour page draws no Exit point group at all. The page shows no exit row and no "not taken" line.

   The PR causes the failure. With only `Threading => role == PickRole::Start` put back in `pick_kinds.rs`, the same test passes (1 passed, 0 failed).

   This is also a user-visible gap. An exit pick that MCP sets, or that a project file loads, changes the posted path. The Wire Contour page cannot show it and cannot clear it.

   Fix (one of these, the author decides):
   - Add an Exit point group with rows to the Wire Contour Geometry tab (beside `wire_start_group`), so a user can see, set and clear the exit. Update the test to assert the rows.
   - Or, as the smallest change: show the stated exit on the Wire Contour page and let the user clear it. Update the test.

   The two fixes change `crates/ui`. Thus the body must then have before/after screenshots of the Wire Contour Geometry tab, on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch. Run `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` from `crates/ui` on the new head, and name the test in the body.

   If the UI row stays a follow-up, file the follow-up issue and name it in the body. The body now says "The row is a follow-up" with no issue number.

## What looks good

- The open run is walked the other way on the same points. The wire-centre path has no G41/G42 (the wire posts write the centre path), so the kerf stays on the same side.
- The closed profile keeps the full automatic lap byte for byte. The ride after the lap follows the ring index order, which is the order of `ring::walk_from`, so it stays in the burnt kerf. The lead-out goes from the nearest point of the wire path to the pick, so it stays on the waste side. `laws::kerf` judges the result again.
- Each refused pair is refused at the command door and at generation. `cond.skims` comes from `op.skims` (`wire_op.rs:122-127`), so no skim path can skip the exit refusal.
- No recorded program changed: `git diff --stat upstream/main...HEAD -- "*.nc" "*.cl" examples testdata assets` is empty.
- Decision file, `Changelog:` line, `Fixes #3332`, conventional subjects, provenance line on `exit.rs`: present. No process file changed.

## Results merged with main (locally)

PR head `309c05314` already contains `upstream/main` `ddee3aed6`. The trial merge was "Already up to date".

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib wire_edm` | 77 passed |
| `app: wire_post`, `wire_dxf_selection`, `mcp_wire_contour`, `start_exit_shared`, `wire_contour` | 18, 8, 9, 4, 8 passed |

| `app: lib`, `mcp_doc_drift`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `mcp_generate` | all passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` (from `crates/ui`) | **1639 passed, 1 failed** (above) |

Extra suites run: `camcraft-ui --lib` (the full suite). The diff changes no `testdata/` file and no importer code, so the extra fixture and importer rules add no other suite.

Heavy lanes: not run. No heavy record names this head. The author ran the three wire heavy steps on `94e3c5df2`. Heavy lanes are not a merge condition.

## Mutations (repeated locally)

1. `exit_side` result ignored in `closed()` (exit side law off): red - `each_exit_pick_a_closed_profile_cannot_hold_is_refused_by_name` (motion) and `exit_pick::each_exit_pick_the_wire_cannot_hold_is_refused_by_name` (app).
2. Open run turn inverted (`da > db`): red - `an_open_run_ends_at_the_end_nearest_the_exit_pick` (motion) and `exit_pick::an_exit_pick_on_an_open_run_ends_the_cut_at_the_end_nearest_the_pick` (app).
3. `Threading` takes the start only (the old capability): the UI test above passes.

All sources were restored. The worktree has no changes.

## Optional, non-blocking

- `crates/app/src/operation/wire_op.rs` grows from 496 to 506 lines. The body gives the reason (overlap with #3617).
- On a closed profile, when the foot of the exit pick is on the seam edge behind the threading foot, the wire rides one more full lap in its kerf. This is safe, but it is long. A note in the path notes could say so.
